summary: Task-3 implemented per plan within its allowed-file scope. All four in-scope acceptance criteria verified empirically on reviewed commit 0d647a2; all runnable verification gates pass (test_cpu_engine + test_rb_fail_closed 105 passed; property tests 9 passed; mocked 2-core BACKTEST_BATCH_WORKERS/resolve checks correct; numba.get_num_threads()==2 with env set pre-import; setdefault preserves user overrides). STOP conditions checked and none triggered (no 0/>cpu_count workers on 2-core mock; ForbiddenProcessPool guard test green). Acceptance item 'RB Governor + island scheduler cap parallelism to 2 and log once' is only partially met: rb_governor.py provably contains no executor usage (sequential loops), so there was nothing to cap there (task evidence line was stale), but the sole remaining concurrent CPU-heavy path (CvFoldValEvaluator fold pool, phases/phase2_rule_pool.py:742, max_workers=len(engines)) is bounded only implicitly by the PURGED_WF_N_SPLITS=2 default and lives in a file excluded from this task's allowed list - recorded as non-blocking MEDIUM F-1 requiring a plan/scope decision (follow-up task or reconcile note), not an implementer fix inside this isolation branch. No HIGH findings.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: On cpu_count==2 BACKTEST_BATCH_WORKERS resolves to 2 (or avoids fork when JAX already loaded); RB/Phase2 batch eval max_workers = min(2, BACKTEST_BATCH_WORKERS); no in-scope code path spawns >2 concurrent CPU-heavy workers
acceptance_criteria.evidence: resolve_backtest_workers (gpu_fuzzy_trader/config.py:382-401): cpus<=2 -> hw_cap=min(2,cpus), requested bounded by hw_cap with floor 1 (never 0, never >cpu_count). Mocked os.cpu_count=2: BACKTEST_BATCH_WORKERS=2, resolve()=2, resolve(16)=2, resolve(1)=1 (verified live). Constant now derives from helper (config.py:404). cpu_engine.simulate_rule_set_batch derives workers from resolve_backtest_workers both for default (cpu_engine.py:1224) and explicit max_workers callers (cpu_engine.py:1226, clamped by hardware cap - semantics change affects no production caller; grep shows zero explicit max_workers call sites outside tests). '(or 1 when JAX loaded)' satisfied in spirit: worker count stays at cap but the pool switches to ThreadPoolExecutor under _jax_runtime_loaded() (cpu_engine.py:1237-1244), eliminating the fork hazard the parenthetical targets.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Numba respects NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=min(2,cpu_count) set before numba import and enforced via numba.set_num_threads(); numba.get_num_threads()==2
acceptance_criteria.evidence: _jax_env.configure_jax_env() setdefaults NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=min(2,cpus) (gpu_fuzzy_trader/_jax_env.py:60-69). Production ordering verified: run_pipeline.py:98-100 calls configure_jax_env() before any module-level numba import reaches it (reporter/phase5/phase2/rb_governor/selector module-level chains contain no evolution import; evox_runner->numba_ops is reached only via function-local imports at phases/phase2_rule_pool.py:2534,3488,3635,4141,4236; gpu_engine.py:45 also calls configure_jax_env at module top). Enforcement after import: numba_ops.py:18-28 reads NUMBA_NUM_THREADS and calls numba.set_num_threads (guarded try/except, '' env handled via `or 0`). Verified live: NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=2 -> get_num_threads()==2. Caveat for direct-library entry paths recorded as LOW F-2.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: cpu_engine chooses ThreadPool when jax in sys.modules else ProcessPool, worker count from centralized helper, no ad-hoc os.cpu_count duplication
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Guard chain intact: cache-path ThreadPool (cpu_engine.py:1233), _jax_runtime_loaded() -> ThreadPool with debug log (cpu_engine.py:1237-1244), else ProcessPoolExecutor with thread-fallback on failure (cpu_engine.py:1247-1252). Worker count exclusively via config.resolve_backtest_workers (cpu_engine.py:1224-1226); no new os.cpu_count() call sites added anywhere in diff. STOP-condition test test_rule_set_batch_avoids_process_fork_when_jax_is_loaded (tests/unit/test_cpu_engine.py:79-99) monkeypatches _jax_runtime_loaded True and swaps ProcessPoolExecutor for a raising ForbiddenProcessPool - passes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMEXPR (+NUMBA) default 2 on 2-core via os.environ.setdefault in _jax_env early import, without overwriting user settings
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Loop over the five env vars with os.environ.setdefault(env_var, str(max(1,min(2,cpus)))) (_jax_env.py:59-69) placed at the top of configure_jax_env(), which both production entries invoke before heavy imports (run_pipeline.py:100, gpu_engine.py:45). Verified live: fresh process -> all five vars = 2; presetting OMP_NUM_THREADS=7 then re-calling configure_jax_env keeps 7 (user settings never overwritten).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: RB Governor + island scheduler cap parallelism to 2 and log once
acceptance_criteria.evidence: RB Governor itself spawns nothing concurrent: repo-wide executor grep shows zero ThreadPool/ProcessPool usage in rb_governor.py; every rule-set evaluation is a sequential simulate_rule_set loop (rb_governor.py:852-884, 1107-1108, 1196 list comprehension) - so <=2 holds trivially and the task's evidence bullet about pools in rb_governor.py was stale; no edit needed there. However the only remaining concurrent CPU-heavy path, CvFoldValEvaluator's fold pool (phases/phase2_rule_pool.py:741-743, ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(engines))), is NOT bounded by resolve_backtest_workers: it equals the 2-core cap only coincidentally via PURGED_WF_N_SPLITS=2 default (config.py:298); an explicit n_splits>2 spawns >2 concurrent heavy backtests on 2-core. That file is explicitly outside this task's allowed list, so the gap is a plan scope-vs-acceptance contradiction (see F-1). The 'log once' observability of resolved caps was not implemented anywhere either (only the pre-existing JAX-threadpool debug log at cpu_engine.py:1240-1243).

findings.title: Acceptance item 5 partial: CvFoldValEvaluator fold pool unbounded by resolve_backtest_workers; no 'log once' of resolved caps anywhere
findings.detail: ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(engines)) bounds parallelism by CV fold count, not by the centralized worker cap. Under shipped defaults (PURGED_WF_N_SPLITS=2) this equals 2 and the plan invariant 'no code path spawns >2 concurrent CPU-heavy workers' holds on every path (RB sequential; batch eval capped at 2; fold pool = 2). But an explicit n_splits>2 yields len(folds)>2 concurrent full-backtest evaluations on a 2-core host, contradicting acceptance criterion 1's absolute phrasing and criterion 5's island-scheduler cap. This file is excluded from task-3's allowed list (plan Out-of-scope lists phase2_rule_pool while its own acceptance demands the cap), so the implementer could not close it without an isolation violation. Requires orchestrator/plan decision: follow-up task amending scope, or reconcile note accepting default-config behavior. Non-blocking for THIS commit.

findings.title: Numba cap is effective only when configure_jax_env() ran before numba import (true for run_pipeline/gpu_engine entries)
findings.detail: numba_ops reads NUMBA_NUM_THREADS once at import time; if a consumer imports gpu_fuzzy_trader.evolution.* directly without going through an entry point that calls configure_jax_env() first, neither the setdefault nor the set_num_threads applies and numba defaults to all cores (observed: bare `import numba` -> get_num_threads()=16 on this 16-core host). All production entry paths are covered today (run_pipeline.py:100 precedes lazy evolution imports; gpu_engine.py:45 self-configures). Suggest a future hardening: have numba_ops fall back to min(2, os.cpu_count()) when the env var is absent instead of skipping set_num_threads. Non-blocking.

quality_notes: Centralization done right: single source of truth resolve_backtest_workers (config.py:382-401) replaces the ad-hoc min(8, os.cpu_count() or 4) constant; behavior for >2-core hosts is byte-for-byte equivalent to the old formula (min(8,cpus)), so no regression for the RTX 4050/8-core dev baseline.

Explicit max_workers callers are now hardware-clamped (cpu_engine.py:1226) - intentional per acceptance ('no ad-hoc duplication', cap parallelism); audited: zero production callers pass explicit max_workers (only the unit test does, with value 2), so no behavioral surprise.
numba_ops env parsing handles empty-string edge (`or 0`) and ImportError keeps njit=None contract intact; set_num_threads wrapped in try/except so exotic numba builds cannot break import.
_jax_env threading defaults use max(1, min(2, cpus)) guarding cpu_count()-None and single-core hosts consistently with resolve_backtest_workers.
No dead code left behind: old comment block about 8-core scoping replaced; no stale references to the previous constant semantics found in touched files.
New test covers boundary matrix {1,2,4,16} x {default, over-cap request, under-cap request} - matches STOP-condition guards.
